answer.text: Selling losing positions to realise capital losses offsetting gains (legitimate, subject to Section 94(7) wash-sale)

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax-loss harvesting at year-end is a legitimate tax-planning technique: realising losses on losing positions creates capital losses that can be set off against capital gains under the Income Tax Act, subject to the usual set-off / carry-forward rules. Indian rules around 'bonus stripping' and 'dividend stripping' (Section 94(7)/(8)) restrict gaming the strategy via near-simultaneous repurchase around record dates. The Trap: 'Always illegal' is wrong because realising a genuine loss is a recognised tax event; 'random' is not a tax characterisation; 'prohibited by SEBI' confuses SEBI (market regulator) with the income-tax regime — SEBI does not generally prohibit how a taxpayer recognises gains and losses. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook pages checked (pp. 185-190 and 237) cover PMS tax streams and discuss a US-context wash-sale / January-effect anomaly, but do not present year-end tax-loss harvesting or Section 94(7) as a named Indian PMS technique. The framing above is general Indian tax-planning knowledge rather than a workbook quote.
